newsitem.title: USA: CBOT wheat closes higher on exports, slow harvest.
newsitem.headline: CBOT wheat closes higher on exports, slow harvest.

text.p: CBOT soft red winter wheat futures closed higher on export news and a harvest slowdown, traders said.

"Algeria took a little piece of U.S. and Pakistan took a lot of U.S. so there's some demand showing up but we're still running behind and need to catch up," said Dave Armstrong, analyst for Chicago-based trade house ABN Amro-Chicago Corp.

U.S. exporters on Thursday said Pakistan bought 500,000 tonnes of wheat with 350,000 of the tally coming from the U.S. Also overnight, Paris-based sources said Algeria bought roughly 275,000 tonnes of wheat, one-half came from the U.S.
U.S. net export sales of wheat during the week ended June 19 totalled 584,100 tonnes, above expectations for 300,000 to 400,000 tonnes.
Activity in the U.S. Great Plains wheat harvest region found favor with wheat bulls.
Joel Burgio, Weather Services Corp meteorologist said many Kansas wheat fields were battered by rain, high winds and hail late Wednesday and more rain was forecast through the weekend.
Wheat closed one to 3-3/4 cents per bushel higher, with July up 1-1/4 at $3.33 a bushel and September closed three cents higher at $3.43.
There are some ideas that wheat may have reached its seasonal harvest lows recently. But analysts, including Armstrong, said the jury's still out on that scenario.
"We can talk about seasonal lows being in but there's nothing dynamic to prove it," Armstrong said.

Prudential Securities bought three million bushels of September, FIMAT Futures bought two million September and Cargill Inc bought 1.5 million bushels of September, traders said. Lind Waldock sold 2.5 million bushels of September, traders said.
In spread trading, ADM Investor Services did one million July/December at 20 cents, premium December and Refco Inc spread one milion July/September at nine cents, premium September, traders said.
Wheat futures volume was estimated by the CBOT at 21,000 contracts, below the 23,391 traded Wednesday.

In wheat options, Refco Inc bought 500 September $3.50 calls at nine cents and sold 500 September $3.80 calls at 2-3/4 cents, traders said. Lind Waldock bought 500 September $3.30 puts and sold 500 September $3.60 calls at even to one cent.
Wheat options volume was estimated at 4,400 contracts.
